traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Cleomaceae: leaves alternate; leaves compound; compound leaves palmate; stipules present; plants hermaphrodite or polygamous; ovary superior; stems usually herbaceous, rarely woody; flowers zygomorphic; perianth sepals and petals; fruit pod; stamens 4 to 50; carpels 2. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); a state the authors qualify (rarely, usually, a share) keeps its word, an unqualified one beside a usual state reads as sometimes.

traits.zygomorphy.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data), family Cleomaceae: its irregular flowers are of no named kind (pea flower, two lips, orchid lip), read from the coded corolla symmetry (spec-rework/b1/delta): zygomorphy other.

traits.leaf_shape.note: POWO, Cleome (Flora Zambesiaca text) (read 2026-10-17): leaflets narrow, linear to lanceolate, 3-9 per leaf; Wikipedia Cleomaceae (read 2026-10-17): palmately compound, mostly 3-7 leaflets, Cleome the largest genus (199 species). Shape is the leaflets'.

traits.leaf_margin.note: POWO, Cleome (read 2026-10-17): leaflets entire or finely serrulate (Cayman Islands and Flora Zambesiaca texts).
